subject: tarantula and frog
title: A Tarantula Lets One Tiny Frog Live in Its Burrow. It Eats the Rest

scenes.text: This tarantula eats frogs. One kind, it lets move in.
In Peru, the dotted humming frog, two centimeters long, shares a burrow with a tarantula.
Young spiders grab the frog, feel it over with their mouthparts, and put it down unharmed.
Other frogs get eaten. This one's skin seems to carry a chemical that says not food.
The frog gets a bodyguard and leftovers. In return, scientists think it eats the ants that raid the spider's eggs.
Nobody has proven that part. But up to four frogs can share one spider's burrow.

description:
In southeastern Peru, a frog about 2 centimetres long, the dotted humming frog, lives in the burrow of a large tarantula that eats other frogs.
First described in 1989: young spiders pick the frog up, examine it with their mouthparts and release it, apparently because of chemicals in its skin. The frog gets shelter, protection and insects drawn to the spider's leftovers; the idea that it repays the spider by eating ants that attack the eggs is still a hypothesis. From one to four frogs have been seen at a single burrow. Similar pairings are reported from India and Sri Lanka.
Strangest animal partnership you know of? Comment below.
first_comment: The frogs stay within about 5 centimetres of the burrow entrance. Would you take a tarantula as a bodyguard?
